answer: Each identity locks a bond on the ledge; weight equals bond squared, so one honest 300-credit bond weighs 90,000. A 14-claim sonnet declaration accompanies each bond; shale auditors recompute weights, and misreported bonds burn. Splitting a pool across k identities divides its weight by k, so matching 90,000 takes 3,000 credits at 100 fakes and 9,487 credits, about 9.5 each, at 1,000 fakes; no bond serves two identities. A weight-splitting ring fails: divided weight cannot outvote honest identities, and double-counted ledge bonds burn. Honest users need one identity, one 300-credit bond.
